counting_note: NA and COVERED count questionnaire functions (leaf questions, with the 26 local-relation rows and their four columns counted as one function per row). CLUMSY/GAP/UNDECIDED/IDEA count the items below; one item often covers several questionnaire functions.

items.source: 2.1.1.2.1.2, 2.1.1.2.2.2 subject that is not an agent
items.what: The spec does not say whether the single argument of an uncontrolled event, or a non-acting transitive subject, is AGENT or THEME.
items.example: I fell; the patient died; the wind broke the window; the key opened the door
items.how_now: spec has both 'arrive AGENT A' and 'fail THEME test'; states take AGENT for the holder; wind could be AGENT, CAUSE or WITH
items.suggestion: One rule: AGENT only for a participant that acts with control (plus experiencers/holders of states); every other sole argument is THEME; forces are CAUSE, instruments WITH. Then fall AGENT x = deliberately, fall THEME x = by accident.

items.source: 2.1.1.2.8, 2.1.1.2.12 objects governed by verbs and adjectives
items.what: No rule or lexicon field fixes which role a root's second argument takes, so writers will pick different roles for the same root.
items.example: help him, wait for her, depend on X, afraid of dogs, proud of it, good at chess, different from B
items.how_now: help THEME x / help TO x / help FOR x all look legal; different THAN x or FROM x
items.suggestion: Give every root in the lexicon a role frame (the roles it takes and what each means), checked by the validator; default second argument = THEME, ABOUT for subject matter.

items.category: state vs change vs caused change
items.what: A property root as predicate can be read as a state, a change into the state, or causing the state, and the spec only defines the first.
items.example: the door is open / the door opens / she opens the door; he became a soldier
items.how_now: open THEME door (state); BEGIN open THEME door probably = becomes open; open AGENT A THEME door is unlicensed and clashes with 'holder of a state is AGENT'
items.suggestion: State it: bare property root = state; BEGIN + root = become; causing needs the cause-to affix (or a CAUSE phrase), never a bare added AGENT. 'Become N' = BEGIN N THEME x.

items.what: There is no stated way to give the resulting or attributed property of the THEME in the same clause.
items.example: we made him king; they painted the door red; I consider it wrong; she was elected chair
items.how_now: block: consider THEME { wrong THEME it }; AS for roles (appoint THEME him AS general); result of 'paint ... red' could be AS, TO or WITH
items.suggestion: Rule: attributed or resulting state always goes in AS (paint THEME door AS red; call THEME it AS error); judgements of a whole proposition use a block.

items.what: It is undecided what a non-thing root means in head position (act, result, doer, quality, or the thing that has the quality) and how ( ) with roles differs from a { } block.
items.example: John's refusal of the offer; the size of the file; the building; the destruction took three days
items.how_now: refuse OF John? (refuse AGENT John THEME offer)? { refuse AGENT John THEME offer }? big OF file = size or 'the big one'?
items.suggestion: Rule: an act root as head = the act/event; a property root as head = the property itself; { } = the proposition/fact; all other readings (doer, product, tool, place, dimension) need a derivational affix. 'The big one' = THAT KIND big.

items.source: 2.1.1.4.1, .3, .11, .13, 2.1.1.5 general; rule 'a role may appear once per clause'
items.what: Several roles each merge two meanings but may occur only once per clause, so a clause that needs both meanings must force them into one AND-phrase.
items.example: I bought it for Bill for his birthday; send the file to Ana to Paris; cut it carefully with a knife
items.how_now: FOR (Bill AND birthday); WITH (knife AND care) - the AND wrongly makes them the same kind of thing
items.suggestion: Allow a role to repeat when its fillers are of different sub-kinds, or split the three busiest pairs (beneficiary/purpose, recipient/end point, means/manner).

items.what: The meaning 'without X' has no fixed form: NOT before a role's phrase can mean 'without X' or 'with something other than X'.
items.example: I hit it without a hammer; I went without Bill; he did it without care
items.how_now: WITH NOT hammer / WITH NONE hammer / ALONG NOT Bill
items.suggestion: Fix: role + NOT phrase = without (no such participant); role + OTHER ... = a different one.

items.what: There is no linker for 'that has X' (the inverse of OF), which technical description uses constantly.
items.example: a man with dirty hands; a function with two arguments; a list with no duplicates
items.how_now: function KIND { have AGENT SELF THEME 2 argument }
items.suggestion: Add one linker HAVING (inverse of OF): function HAVING 2 argument; list HAVING NONE duplicate. This also replaces 'having' and 'lacking' affixes.

items.source: 2.1.1.4.6.3 present vs past possession; nominal tense
items.what: Time particles cannot stand in a modifier, so 'former', 'then', 'future' need a full relative clause.
items.example: the former owner; my future manager; the old value
items.how_now: person KIND { PAST own AGENT SELF THEME house }
items.suggestion: Let a modifier carry a time particle: owner KIND PAST; value KIND PAST; manager KIND FUTURE.

items.what: There are at least three ways to say that something measures so much, and none is named as the standard one.
items.example: the sample weighs 5 kg; a boat of a thousand tons; a table worth five pounds; the run took 3 s
items.how_now: heavy THEME S SPAN 5 «kg» / EQUAL THEME weight OF S THAN 5 «kg» / boat KIND (1000 ton)
items.suggestion: Canonical: dimension root + SPAN measure (heavy THEME S SPAN 5 «kg»), read as neutral (no claim that S is heavy); attributive: boat KIND (heavy SPAN 1000 ton).

items.what: It is unclear whether the unit or the substance is the head in a measured amount.
items.example: a pound of sugar; three cups of water; 20 lines of code
items.how_now: 1 pound KIND sugar / 1 pound sugar (number + unit as quantifier) / sugar KIND (1 pound)
items.suggestion: Rule: number + unit is a quantifier, substance is the head: 3 cup water, 5 «ml» acid.

items.what: The spec does not say which roots are relational (take REL) and which take OF, nor the difference between 'top OF tree' and 'top REL tree'.
items.example: the top of the tree; Ana's friend; the author of the file; the cause of the error; a member of the set
items.how_now: friend REL Ana (spec) but file OF user; top OF tree or top REL tree; cause OF / REL error
items.suggestion: Mark relational roots in the lexicon. Rule: OF = a part or possession of the whole; REL = something defined by its relation to a separate landmark (top OF tree = the treetop, top REL tree = the space above it).

items.what: Selecting some of an already identified set works only when the selector is a number, because quantifiers cannot be heads.
items.example: three of the ten tests; some of the boys; none of them; most of these files
items.how_now: 3 OF (THAT 10 test) works; SOME OF (THAT boy) is not grammatical; SOME THAT boy has no defined reading
items.suggestion: Rule for stacked quantifiers: the left one selects from the set fixed by the rest: SOME THAT boy, 3 THAT 10 test, NONE THAT 2 (neither).

items.source: 2.1.1.4.20 price; 2.1.5.1 other adpositions (instead of, in exchange for)
items.what: No role marks the thing given in exchange or the thing replaced; INSTEAD marks only the chosen item.
items.example: I bought it for two pounds; use tabs instead of spaces; replace X with Y
items.how_now: cannot in one clause; two clauses: use THEME tab AND NOT use THEME space
items.suggestion: Add one role (gloss SWAP): the thing given up, replaced or paid: use THEME tab SWAP space; buy THEME it SWAP 2 pound.

items.what: A non-exhaustive mention of members inside a phrase is not possible: NOTE means 'namely' (exhaustive), EXAMPLE works only between sentences, and EXCEPT is a clause role, not attached to its phrase.
items.example: everyone including John; sugars such as glucose; all tests except login read all files except config
items.how_now: separate EXAMPLE sentence; NOTE (ALSO John) is a guess; two EXCEPTs in one clause are impossible
items.suggestion: Add a linker INCLUDING (non-exhaustive members) and let EXCEPT also be used as a linker after the phrase it limits.

items.what: There is no way to mention a native word or particle as a word rather than use it.
items.example: the word 'test' has two senses; the particle NOT comes first
items.how_now: « » is for foreign text only; DEFINE takes a term but ordinary mention is unspecified
items.suggestion: Parallel to 'name root': a marker meaning 'the word itself', e.g. word root, with « » for longer native quotations.

items.source: 2.1.1.4-6 note (b) copular complement and (c) attributive use; 2.1.1.2.3
items.what: With no 'is' and a predicate that must be a root, it is unclear how to predicate a place, time or owner, or how to attach a role phrase to a noun.
items.example: the file is in the folder; the meeting is at nine; the book is Ana's; the book on the table
items.how_now: exist THEME file AT inside REL folder / (inside REL folder) THEME file; book KIND (top REL table)
items.suggestion: Allow a role phrase in ( ) as predicate and as modifier: (AT inside REL folder) THEME file; book KIND (AT top REL table); (OF Ana) THEME book.

items.what: Direction of motion with no landmark, and 'toward' as opposed to 'as far as', have no stated form.
items.example: go up; move back; walk toward the city; scroll down
items.how_now: TO up? WITH up? TO toward REL city?
items.suggestion: Rule: a relational root with no REL after TO/FROM/VIA is a pure direction (go TO up); TO = reaching the end point, TO (toward REL city) = direction only.

items.what: The particle glossed ALONG means companion, while English 'along' is a path, so a writer working from the gloss will misuse it for paths.
items.example: walk along the river vs walk with Bill
items.how_now: ALONG Bill (companion); VIA along REL river (path)
items.suggestion: Rename the gloss to COMPANION (or ACCOMPANY) so no particle gloss collides with a needed relational root.

items.what: The notation for clock times and calendar dates is not fixed; the spec's own 'day KIND five' and 'before REL 9' are ambiguous.
items.example: at 7 o'clock; on Monday; in January 1976
items.how_now: WHEN 9 / WHEN «07:00» / WHEN day KIND five / roots for weekday and month names
items.suggestion: Dates and clock times always in « » ISO form (WHEN «1976-01», WHEN «07:00»); weekdays and months as unit root + ORD (weekday ORD 1).

items.what: 'Ago', 'in two hours' and 'within the last hour' need a deictic 'now' landmark that the spec does not provide as a head.
items.example: I was here two hours ago; back in two hours; five calls in the last hour
items.how_now: WHEN (before SPAN 2 hour REL ?now) - NOW is a time particle, not a head; SPAN alone would mean duration
items.suggestion: Generalise NEAR/FAR: a measure may follow PAST or FUTURE (PAST 2 hour = two hours ago; FUTURE 2 hour = in two hours; PAST ATMOST 1 hour = within the last hour).

items.what: Start and end of a period can be said with WHEN + relational root or with FROM/TO, and the spec does not choose.
items.example: since Monday; from Monday to Friday; until the release
items.how_now: WHEN since REL monday / FROM monday TO friday / WHEN until REL release
items.suggestion: Allow FROM and TO for time bounds as for space, keep WHEN for the point or frame; drop 'since' and 'until' from the relational roots.

items.source: 2.1.1.6 note on tense restrictions; 2.1.3.2.1.1-2 universal and present tense
items.what: Unmarked is defined as timeless, yet the spec's first example uses it for a present observation, and nothing says whether tense is needed when WHEN gives the time or in every STORY sentence.
items.example: the login test fails (now) vs login tests fail (always); yesterday he left
items.how_now: 'GIVEN fail THEME test KIND login' = fails now, contrary to the rule; PAST must be repeated in each narrative sentence
items.suggestion: Rule: unmarked = timeless only under RECALLED/RULE/DEFINE and with GENERIC; under GIVEN it is the time of observation; an absolute WHEN makes PAST/FUTURE optional.

items.what: SOME is not defined as 'at least one, possibly all' or 'some but not all', which matters for inference.
items.example: some tests fail (do all fail?)
items.how_now: SOME test
items.suggestion: Define SOME = at least one, no claim about the rest; 'not all' is written NOT ALL; 'a few' is SEVERAL or FEW.

items.what: A particular but unidentified referent is not clearly distinguished from 'some or other'.
items.example: I am looking for a (certain) book vs any book
items.how_now: ANY book (nonspecific) vs SOME book / 1 book / book NAMED B
items.suggestion: State that a phrase with NAMED or a number is specific, ANY is nonspecific, bare is open.

items.what: The spec does not say whether a missing role means 'unspecified someone/something' or 'the one understood from context'.
items.example: Has the release been sent? / He ate. / (dialogue) Sent.
items.how_now: ASK DONE send THEME release (agent unknown) - but a writer may also drop a known agent
items.suggestion: Rule: an omitted role is always unspecified, never a hidden pronoun; known referents need a handle, THAT, ME or YOU. Fragments only after ASK, SOCIAL, HEAD.

items.what: Inclusive 'we' has a form (ME AND YOU) but exclusive 'we' has none.
items.example: we (not you) have decided
items.how_now: ME AND OTHER person / US plus a second clause
items.suggestion: Document US EXCEPT YOU (if EXCEPT becomes a linker) or leave as is.

items.what: SELF is defined for a role of a main clause with an AGENT and for relative clauses, but not inside a phrase, in a clause with no AGENT, or in a complement block.
items.example: the file refers to itself; she washed her own hands; A wants to go; A says he (A) will win
items.how_now: refer THEME file TO SELF (no AGENT); hand OF SELF; want AGENT A THEME { go AGENT A } repeats the handle
items.suggestion: Rule: outside a modifying clause SELF = the AGENT of the nearest clause, else its THEME, at any depth inside that clause's phrases; in a complement block SELF = that same participant (want AGENT A THEME { go AGENT SELF }).

items.what: 'The same X' and 'such X' as modifiers have no stated form; only OTHER exists.
items.example: A and B call the same function; the same error as yesterday; such errors
items.how_now: function KIND EQUAL? call THEME 1 function? error KIND (THAN THAT)
items.suggestion: Add quantifier SAME as the partner of OTHER (SAME function; SAME error THAN ...); 'such' = KIND THAT.

items.what: WHAT in the quantifier slot means both 'which' and 'how many'.
items.example: which tests failed? / how many tests failed?
items.how_now: fail THEME WHAT test (both readings)
items.suggestion: WHAT before the head = how many only; which = head KIND WHAT (already used in the spec's fragment example).

items.source: 2.1.3.1.2.1 intransitive from transitive by not specifying the subject
items.what: 'It happened by itself' and 'someone unnamed did it' are written the same way.
items.example: the water boiled / the water was boiled; the process stopped / was stopped
items.how_now: boil THEME water for both; add CAUSE SELF or AGENT NONE to force 'by itself'
items.suggestion: Falls out of the state/change rule: bare root = happens with no causer implied; root + cause-to with no AGENT = someone did it.

items.what: The CAUSE role already makes a causative of any clause without a second AGENT, so clause-level causation needs no new device.
items.example: the heat melted the ice; the patch made the test fail; I made him eat
items.how_now: cause AGENT ME THEME { eat AGENT A THEME fish } or eat AGENT A THEME fish CAUSE ME
items.suggestion: Declare CAUSE + phrase the standard causative for events; keep the cause-to affix only for building lexical words (kill, heat, teach, show).

items.what: Whether two time particles may stack in a main clause for future-in-past or past-in-future is not stated, though the scope rule implies it.
items.example: he was going to leave; it will have finished
items.how_now: PAST FUTURE leave / FUTURE DONE finish / FUTURE PAST finish - implied only
items.suggestion: State it: the first time particle sets the reference time, the next is counted from it.

items.source: 2.1.3.3.1.3.2 experiential perfect; 2.1.3.3.2.1.8-9 iterative, semelfactive; 2.1.6.5 numeral derivatives
items.what: No role or slot gives how many times something happens, nor 'ever / at least once'.
items.example: the test failed 3 times out of 10; have you ever seen it; twice a week
items.how_now: SPAN 3 time (stretching SPAN) or a count predicate on a nominalised event
items.suggestion: Let a number + TIMES stand in the aspect group: PAST 3 TIMES fail; ATLEAST 1 TIMES = ever; rates as 2 TIMES SPAN week.

items.what: 'Usually' or 'by default' falls between OFTEN and ALWAYS and it is unclear whether HABIT carries it.
items.example: the service usually restarts within a minute
items.how_now: HABIT restart / OFTEN restart / GENERIC on the noun
items.suggestion: Define HABIT as 'as a rule, exceptions allowed' (the clause partner of GENERIC).

items.what: A proposal for joint action has no fixed opener.
items.example: let's run the tests first; shall we stop here?
items.how_now: REQUEST run AGENT (ME AND YOU) / PLAN ... AGENT US / ASK SHOULD ...
items.suggestion: State: REQUEST with AGENT (ME AND YOU) = let's; a mere suggestion = CLAIM SHOULD.

items.what: A wish or hope needs a full 'hope' clause; the attitude list has GLAD and REGRET, which presuppose the fact.
items.example: hopefully the build passes; if only it had worked
items.how_now: CLAIM hope AGENT ME THEME { FUTURE pass THEME build }
items.suggestion: Add attitude HOPE (wanted, not known to be so); with UNREAL it gives 'if only'.

items.what: There is no marked way to warn, which an assistant does often.
items.example: careful: this deletes all data; it may break if you upgrade
items.how_now: CLAIM EMPHASIS delete ... / REQUEST careful AGENT YOU CAUSE { ... }
items.suggestion: Add attitude WARN (the addressee should take care about this), or a relation of the same name.

items.what: CAN covers both ability and factual possibility, but MUST is defined only as 'required', so factual or logical necessity has no clear form.
items.example: the list must be sorted for binary search to work; a prime above 2 must be odd; the function needs two arguments
items.how_now: MUST (rule?) / CERTAIN (writer's confidence) / root need
items.suggestion: Define MUST as the dual of CAN: required by a rule or necessary in fact; the source goes in CAUSE or FOR ('needed for').

items.what: Inference from appearance, with no earlier sentence to cite, fits neither GIVEN nor DERIVED.
items.example: it seems the cache is stale; apparently he left
items.how_now: LIKELY ... / DERIVED with no labels / root seem with a block
items.suggestion: Allow DERIVED with no labels to mean 'inferred from what is seen, grounds unstated'.

items.source: 2.1.3.7 strings of verbs; body = clause AND clause
items.what: It is undecided whether roles and pre-predicate particles of the first clause carry over to clauses joined by AND/OR/BUT.
items.example: A took the file and deleted it; he came, saw and left
items.how_now: PAST take AGENT A THEME F AND PAST delete AGENT A THEME F (full repetition) - or does PAST reach across AND?
items.suggestion: State that nothing carries across AND between clauses, and that a coordinated predicate shares everything: PAST (take AND delete) AGENT A THEME F (already grammatical).

items.what: The set a superlative ranges over has no assigned role.
items.example: the fastest of the three runs; the largest file in the folder
items.how_now: MOST fast THEME R THAN? / OF? / among REL (ALL 3 run)
items.suggestion: Rule: with MOST/LEAST, THAN names the comparison set (MOST fast THEME R THAN ALL 3 run); attributive: file KIND (MOST big) OF folder.

items.what: 'The more X, the more Y' and 'Y grows with X' have no direct form.
items.example: the larger the input, the slower the run; pressure rises with temperature
items.how_now: IF { MORE big THEME input } { MORE slow THEME run }
items.suggestion: Bless that IF { MORE } { MORE } pattern as the standard form, with a factor allowed (2 MORE); exact laws go in « ».

items.what: The maximal-degree-within-limits meaning has no stated form.
items.example: as soon as possible; as small as it can be
items.how_now: MOST early? (EQUAL early THAN { CAN })?
items.suggestion: Rule: MOST + root with THAN { CAN } omitted is plain superlative; write CAN MOST early for 'as early as possible'.

items.what: A degree defined by its actual result needs two sentences or loses the degree link.
items.example: the file is so big that the upload failed
items.how_now: VERY big THEME file . RESULT PAST fail THEME upload .
items.suggestion: State that ENOUGH/TOO ... FOR { block with real time } asserts the result (ENOUGH big FOR { PAST fail THEME upload }).

items.what: Opposition ('against') has no role and FOR has no stated negative.
items.example: vote against the plan; protect against loss; lean against the wall
items.how_now: FOR NOT plan? THEME? a relational root?
items.suggestion: Fix THEME for the thing opposed (oppose THEME plan; protect THEME data FROM loss) and record it in the role frames; no new role.

items.what: A block modifier is described only as a relative clause with SELF; the reading with no SELF (content) is not stated.
items.example: the assumption that the list is sorted; the fact that it failed; the risk of losing data
items.how_now: assume KIND { sorted THEME list }
items.suggestion: State: KIND + block with no SELF gives the content of the head.

items.what: number = digits only, so decimals, negatives, fractions and percentages have no defined place in quantifier or number slots.
items.example: 30% of users; half the files; 3.5 times faster; -2
items.how_now: «30%» OF user? «0.5» file? AROUND «3.5»?
items.suggestion: Let number include decimal, sign, fraction and percent forms; a fraction or percent before a head is partitive (30% THAT user; 1/2 file).

items.category: last, next, nth from the end
items.what: ORD n counts only from the start and there is no ordinal for last, next, previous or 'second largest'.
items.example: the last line; the next step; the second largest value
items.how_now: roots last / next REL x; ORD 2 with (MOST big)?
items.suggestion: ORD LAST, ORD LAST 2 (second from end); next/previous as relational roots; ORD 2 before MOST = second largest.

items.what: Degree particles may stand only before a predicate or modifier, so comparative and excessive quantities, 'almost all', and strict 'more than n' cannot be written in the quantifier slot.
items.example: more errors than yesterday; too many files; enough memory; almost all tests; more than 5 seconds
items.how_now: predicate on a count: MORE big THEME count OF error THAN ...; ATLEAST 6 only works for whole numbers
items.suggestion: Allow {degree} before a quantifier or number: MORE MANY error THAN ..., TOO MANY file, ENOUGH memory, ALMOST ALL test, MORE 5 second, 2 EQUAL MANY.

derivation_functions.subtypes: collective (group of), member/unit, person associated with, place of, abstract status (-hood, -ship), diminutive/augmentative, female/male/young, opposite/non-
derivation_functions.handled_by: group-of, one-who, place-of, quality-of, opposite; size and sex by KIND + root; non- by NOT

derivation_functions.subtypes: act/event, doer, thing done or produced, instrument, place, manner
derivation_functions.handled_by: bare root as head = act; one-who, thing-done, tool-for, place-of; manner = way KIND { }

derivation_functions.subtypes: keeps clause roles or takes noun linkers
derivation_functions.handled_by: undecided: ( root + roles ) keeps roles; affixed words should take OF/KIND only

derivation_functions.subtypes: abstract quality, neutral dimension (length, age), one that is X
derivation_functions.handled_by: quality-of; 'the X one' = THAT KIND x

derivation_functions.subtypes: use as tool, provide with, remove, act as, turn into
derivation_functions.handled_by: no affix: roots are classless (hammer THEME nail); turn into = cause-to; act as = AS

derivation_functions.subtypes: causative, anticausative, reversive, repetitive, reciprocal, reflexive, attempt
derivation_functions.handled_by: cause-to, opposite; AGAIN, MUTUAL, SELF, omission of AGENT, root try

derivation_functions.subtypes: having, lacking, like, pertaining to, made of
doing, done, able to be done, tending to
manner, time, place adverbs from any class
derivation_functions.handled_by: no affix: WITH / WHEN / AT + root
ORD, number + degree, name root; mention marker undecided
role + relational root + REL (FROM behind REL car); no affix
head + KIND + modifier, nested with ( ); fixed terms via DEFINE. Undecided: whether a fixed compound is one lexicon entry and how it differs from a free KIND phrase

derivation.meaning: The other pole of a scale or state; on an action root, the action that undoes it. Not the same as NOT (NOT big is merely 'not big'). Halves the property vocabulary.
derivation.example: big + opposite = small; tie + opposite = untie; before + opposite = after

derivation.meaning: Adds a causer (AGENT) to a state or event root; the former sole argument stays THEME. Repeatable.
derivation.example: die + cause-to = kill; know + cause-to = inform/teach; hot + cause-to = heat

derivation.meaning: The AGENT participant as a thing-word: the person or thing that does the act, or is characterised by the root.
derivation.example: teach + one-who = teacher; science + one-who = scientist

derivation.meaning: The THEME participant or product: what is made, done or undergoes the act.
derivation.example: build + thing-done = building; write + thing-done = text; eat + thing-done = food

derivation.meaning: The WITH participant: the instrument or means made for the act.
derivation.example: cut + tool-for = knife; compute + tool-for = computer

derivation.meaning: The AT participant: the place where the act is done or the thing is kept.
derivation.example: cook + place-of = kitchen; book + place-of = library

derivation.meaning: The abstract property or neutral dimension of a property root, or the state of being X for a thing root.
derivation.example: long + quality-of = length; hot + quality-of = temperature; friend + quality-of = friendship

derivation.meaning: A collection of X taken as one unit (the lexical partner of WHOLE).
derivation.example: tree + group-of = forest; star + group-of = constellation; word + group-of = vocabulary

derivation.meaning: Optional ninth: the property of being able to undergo the act (short for KIND { CAN ... THEME SELF }); frequent in technical prose.
derivation.example: read + can-be = readable; break + can-be = fragile; see + can-be = visible

derivation_note: Design principle behind one-who / thing-done / tool-for / place-of: each picks out one role of the root (AGENT, THEME, WITH, AT). If more are wanted later (recipient, time, reason) they should follow the same pattern rather than be invented ad hoc. Not needed as affixes because the grammar already does the work: become (BEGIN), again (AGAIN), not/non- (NOT), having/lacking (proposed HAVING linker, NOT), like (THAN), -ish/very (SLIGHT, VERY), reflexive/reciprocal (SELF, MUTUAL), adverb-forming (WITH + root), diminutive/augmentative and sex (KIND + root), act-of (bare root as head, once item 5 is decided).

lexicon_fields.field: 5.1.1 kinship
lexicon_fields.note: Small core only: parent, child, sibling, spouse, plus male/female as ordinary roots (mother = parent KIND female). All are relational roots (REL). By marriage/adoption/fostering = KIND + root (marry, adopt). No gendered or generational series needed.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.1.2 colour
lexicon_fields.note: Basic terms only (black, white, red, yellow, green, blue; perhaps brown, grey). Finer shades by KIND, SLIGHT/VERY, or « » codes. 'opposite' could give black from white but is not recommended for hues.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.1.3 body parts
lexicon_fields.note: Largest closed field in the basic list (about 30: head, eye, ear, nose, mouth, tooth, tongue, neck, hand, foot, leg, knee, back, belly, breast, heart, liver, guts, skin, hair, bone, blood, flesh, fat, tail, wing, horn, claw, feather). Part-whole by OF. Low priority for reasoning, needed for everyday talk.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.1.4 cooking
lexicon_fields.note: A few roots (cook, bake, fry); boil, heat, cool, dry, freeze come from state roots + BEGIN or cause-to.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.1.5 other structured fields: knowing and reasoning
lexicon_fields.note: Not in the questionnaire list but the main field for this language: know, think, believe, doubt, prove, infer, assume, mean, cause, result, reason, evidence, true, error. Openers and strength mark the writer's own stance; roots are still needed to talk about others' reasoning.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.1.5 other: speech and social acts
lexicon_fields.note: say, ask, answer, promise, thank, greet, agree, sorry, ok - needed as fillers of SOCIAL and for reported speech.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.1.5 other: generic heads
lexicon_fields.note: thing, person, place, time, way, kind, part, amount, number, event - required because WHAT, ANY, NONE, THIS need a head (who = WHAT person, nowhere = AT NONE place, what he said = thing KIND { }).

lexicon_fields.field: 5.1.5 other: technical and scientific terms
lexicon_fields.note: A general core (data, file, test, value, set, function, measure, force, energy, cell...); the rest by KIND compounds, DEFINE, or « » loans.

lexicon_fields.field: 4.1 ideophones
lexicon_fields.note: None; sound-symbolic words have no place in a written, sound-free language.

lexicon_fields.field: 4.2 interjections
lexicon_fields.note: Done by SOCIAL + root, YES/NO fragments and attitude particles (SURPRISE, GLAD, ANNOYED). No irregular forms; needs only the social-act roots above.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 pronouns (I, thou, he, we, ye, they)
lexicon_fields.note: ME, YOU, US; third person by handles, THAT, or repeating the noun; plural 'you' by a quantifier (ALL YOU, 2 YOU).

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 demonstratives and deictic adverbs (this, that, here, there)
lexicon_fields.note: THIS / THAT + generic head (THIS place = here). Open point: today/yesterday/tomorrow and 'now' as a head need either roots or the proposed PAST/FUTURE + measure.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 question words (what, who, when, where, how)
lexicon_fields.note: WHAT in a role or slot: AGENT WHAT person, AT WHAT, WHEN WHAT, WITH WHAT, CAUSE WHAT, degree WHAT.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 quantifiers and numerals (all, many, few, some, other, one to five)
lexicon_fields.note: Quantifier particles and digits; ordinals by ORD. Roots needed only for collective units (pair, dozen) if wanted.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 grammatical words (and, at, because, if, not, with)
lexicon_fields.note: AND, AT, CAUSE, IF, NOT, WITH/ALONG are particles.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 spatial relations (in, near, far, leftside, rightside, back)
lexicon_fields.note: Grammar gives the frame (AT/TO/FROM/VIA + root + REL) but the relational roots must exist: inside, near, top, above, front, side, left, between, among, around, across, along, beyond. With 'opposite', about half suffice (outside, far, below, behind, right). Same roots serve time (before, after, during).

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 dimension and property words (big, long, wide, thick, heavy, small, short, narrow, thin, new, old, good, bad, warm, cold, wet, dry, full, dirty, sharp, dull, smooth, straight, round, rotten, right/correct)
lexicon_fields.note: One pole per scale; the other by 'opposite'; dimension nouns (length, weight, age, temperature) by quality-of. Watch root/particle doublets: full vs FULL, near/far vs NEAR/FAR, other vs OTHER, many/few vs MANY/FEW should not also be roots.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 people (person, man/male, woman, child, husband, wife, father, mother, name)
lexicon_fields.note: person, male, female, child, spouse, parent, name; the gendered items are KIND compounds.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 animals (animal, bird, dog, fish, louse, snake, worm)
lexicon_fields.note: Open class: a handful of life-form roots, the rest as KIND compounds or « » scientific names.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 plants and plant parts (tree, grass, leaf, root, bark, flower, fruit, seed, stick, woods)
lexicon_fields.note: woods = tree + group-of; bark = skin OF tree if wanted.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 nature, sky, weather, substances (sun, moon, star, sky, cloud, rain, snow, ice, fog, wind, water, sea, lake, river, earth, sand, stone, dust, mountain, fire, smoke, ashes, salt)
lexicon_fields.note: Core roots needed; several reducible (ice = water KIND solid, lake/sea by size, ashes = thing-done of burn).

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 time units (day, night, year)
lexicon_fields.note: Unit roots (second ... year, day, night, season); weekday and month names should be unit + ORD, clock times and dates in « », so no name roots.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 body processes, perception, mind (breathe, eat, drink, bite, suck, spit, vomit, sleep, live, die, laugh, sing, play, see, hear, smell, fear, know, think, say, count, swell)
lexicon_fields.note: All need roots; each needs a role frame (experiencer = AGENT). kill = die + cause-to; show = see + cause-to.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 posture and motion (come, walk, fly, swim, fall, float, flow, turn, lie, sit, stand)
lexicon_fields.note: Manner-of-motion roots needed; come/go is one root with TO/FROM (come = move TO ME), up/down by direction roots.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 handling and impact (give, hold/take, throw, push, pull, hit, cut, split, stab, scratch, rub, wipe, wash, squeeze, tie, sew, dig, hunt, fight, kill, burn, freeze)
lexicon_fields.note: Mostly roots. Free role order removes converse pairs (give/receive, buy/sell are one root each); pull = push + opposite; freeze/burn from state roots with BEGIN or cause-to.

lexicon_fields.field: 5.2 artefacts (road, rope)
lexicon_fields.note: Open class; many derivable with tool-for and place-of.
